# Xōlōtl: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Xōlōtl** is what the evidence put back.

Xōlōtl's myths run on twoness: twin of the morning star, guide of the dying sun, the god who is always the second of a pair — and always the one who goes down into the dark. The Aztec dead journeyed four years through Mictlān's nine levels, and at the deep river it was the dog — Xōlōtl's creature — who swam them across; a soul whose family had mistreated dogs in life found no ferryman.  The funeral rite buried a red dog with the dead: the god's own form, sacrificed to carry its master home.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Xōlōtl
- **ASCII form:** xolotl
- **Meaning:** "The double, the monster"
- **Domain of influence:** Evening Star, Death, Twins
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 266 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Xōlōtl** to *xolotl* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **o → ō** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ō** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Xōlōtl** lives at [/sites/xolotl/](/sites/xolotl/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/xolotl/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/xolotl/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/xolotl/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Xōlōtl** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — The dog who swims the dead across; the oldest companion at the grave.
- **Pet Care & Animal Industries** — The xoloitzcuintli: Mexico’s national dog, named for its god.
- **Biotech, Longevity & Life Sciences** — His axolotl regenerates limbs and heart — the mascot of regenerative medicine.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/xolotl/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
